name: Ninh Binh
region: Southern Red River Delta, northern Vietnam
tagline: Ha Long Bay on land: limestone towers rising from rice paddies and rivers, explored by rowing boat, bicycle and mountain stairway, with an ancient capital hidden among them.
highlight: A rowing boat gliding through a cave beneath the cliffs at Trang An, with water buffalo grazing beside the river.
shortDescription: A landscape of karst hills, rivers, caves and paddies two hours south of Hanoi, with the boat trips of Trang An and Tam Coc, the Hang Mua viewpoint, Hoa Lu ancient capital and Bai Dinh pagoda.
metaDescription: A Ninh Binh travel guide: Trang An and Tam Coc boat trips, Hang Mua viewpoint, Hoa Lu ancient capital, Bai Dinh Pagoda, cycling, best time and a two-day plan from Hanoi.
knownFor: Karst landscapes, boat rides, Hoa Lu, rice paddies, Bai Dinh
goodFor: Scenery, cycling, boat rides, photography, an easy escape from Hanoi

intro: Ninh Binh sits at the southern edge of the Red River Delta, where the flat rice country suddenly gives way to limestone towers, caves and rivers. It was the site of Hoa Lu, the capital of Vietnam under the Dinh and Early Le dynasties in the 10th century, before the court moved to Thang Long, the site of today's Hanoi. Its hills and caves were used as fortresses and hiding places, and the Trang An Landscape Complex, listed by UNESCO as a mixed natural and cultural site in 2014, preserves a series of them.

The scenery is often compared with Ha Long Bay, and the comparison holds. Instead of the sea, there are rice paddies, lotus ponds, rivers and lakes, with limestone karsts rising like fingers from the water. Sampans, small rowing boats, take visitors through caves and along channels between the cliffs, often propelled by rowers using their feet. Film crews chose Trang An for Kong: Skull Island in 2017.

Ninh Binh is close to Hanoi, and many visitors come on a day trip, but the pace and light are best appreciated with a night or two. Cycling between the sites, climbing to viewpoints and eating in village restaurants make it one of the most relaxed stops in the north.

whyVisit.intro: Ninh Binh offers the kind of scenery that people go to Ha Long Bay for, with a slower, more rural feel.

points.title: A dramatic landscape
points.text: Karst hills, caves, rivers and rice paddies together make an outstanding backdrop.

points.title: Boat rides
points.text: A journey through caves and along the river at Trang An or Tam Coc is the highlight.

points.title: Viewpoints
points.text: Hang Mua's 500-step climb gives one of the best views in northern Vietnam.

points.title: History
points.text: Hoa Lu, the 10th-century capital, and the huge Bai Dinh Pagoda.

points.title: Easy from Hanoi
points.text: Trains and buses take about two hours.

attractionsIntro: The sights are spread around the province, and are best reached by bicycle, scooter or car.

attractions.name: Trang An Landscape Complex
attractions.text: A network of rivers and caves, explored on rowing boats for two to three hours, passing temples, grottoes and karst peaks. It is the most impressive and best organised boat route.
attractions.tip: Go early, and choose a route with more caves.

attractions.name: Tam Coc

image.alt: A rowing boat on the river at Tam Coc among limestone hills and rice fields

attractions.text: A river route through three caves, whose name means Three Caves, with rice paddies on either side. It is busier and shorter than Trang An, and best in the ripening season.
attractions.tip: Visit in late May or June to see golden rice.

attractions.name: Hang Mua (Mua Cave viewpoint)
attractions.text: A stairway of about 500 steps up a limestone hill, leading to a viewpoint with a dragon statue and a panorama of the rice fields, river and karsts.
attractions.tip: Go early or late, and bring water.

attractions.name: Hoa Lu ancient capital

image.alt: Temple gates and karst hills at Hoa Lu, the ancient capital of Vietnam

attractions.text: The capital of the Dinh and Early Le dynasties from 968 to 1010, with restored temples dedicated to the kings and surrounded by mountains.

attractions.name: Bai Dinh Pagoda

image.alt: The vast Bai Dinh Pagoda complex on a hillside in Ninh Binh

attractions.text: A huge modern Buddhist complex, the largest in Vietnam, with a long corridor of Buddha statues, a giant bronze Buddha and a tall stupa.

attractions.name: Van Long Nature Reserve
attractions.text: A wetland reserve with quiet boat rides among karsts and rare langurs, calmer than Trang An.

thingsToDoIntro: Ninh Binh is best on two wheels and on the water.

thingsToDo.title: Take a boat through Trang An
thingsToDo.text: Sit back as a rower guides you through caves and channels.
thingsToDo.tip: Go in the morning to avoid the crowds.

thingsToDo.title: Climb Hang Mua
thingsToDo.text: See the whole landscape from the top of the stairs.
thingsToDo.tip: Go at sunrise or late afternoon.

thingsToDo.title: Cycle through the countryside
thingsToDo.text: Quiet lanes link paddies, villages and temples.
thingsToDo.tip: Rent a bicycle in Tam Coc.

thingsToDo.title: Try a cooking class
thingsToDo.text: Cook with a local family, using produce from their garden.

thingsToDo.title: Visit Cuc Phuong National Park
thingsToDo.text: Vietnam's oldest national park, with ancient trees and a primate rescue centre.

thingsToDo.title: Sample goat meat and crispy rice
thingsToDo.text: Local specialities of Ninh Binh, at restaurants around town.

foodIntro: Ninh Binh's specialities include goat meat and crispy rice, and its village restaurants serve fresh, simple food.

foods.name: Goat meat dishes
foods.text: Goat prepared in many ways, from steamed to grilled to hotpot, a regional speciality.

foods.name: Com chay (burnt rice)
foods.text: Crispy fried rice served with pork or seafood, a local dish.

foods.name: Snail noodles
foods.text: Rice noodles with river snails, served in a sour broth.

foods.name: Fresh river fish
foods.text: Fish from the local rivers, grilled or steamed.

accommodation.intro: Choose a homestay among the rice fields, or a hotel in Ninh Binh town.

areas.name: Tam Coc
areas.text: Homestays, bungalows and boutique hotels among the paddies.

areas.name: Trang An and Hoa Lu
areas.text: Hotels near the Trang An entrance.

gettingThere.intro: Ninh Binh is about 95 km south of Hanoi.

options.text: About 2 to 2.5 hours on the Reunification line, with several services a day.
About 2 hours from Hanoi, with drop-off in Tam Coc.

gettingAround.intro: The sights are spread out, and cycling is the pleasant way to see them.

options.text: Cheap to rent, and roads are quiet.

options.detail: Wear a helmet, and check your licence and insurance.

options.text: For longer distances such as Bai Dinh.

bestTime.headline: March–June and September–November
bestTime.summary: Ninh Binh follows the northern climate, with cool winters and hot summers. The golden rice season is late May and June.

seasons.text: Hot and humid. Golden rice in late May and June.
Clear skies and a second rice harvest.
Cool, grey and misty, with fewer visitors.

bestTime.avoid: Weekends and public holidays, when Trang An is packed.

itinerary.title: Two days in Ninh Binh
itinerary.intro: The boat trips and the viewpoint on the first day, and history on the second.

tipsIntro: A few tips help you make the most of the area.
tips: Stay a night or two instead of a day trip.
Go to Trang An early, before the tour groups.
Tip the boat rower, who works hard.
Climb Hang Mua at the start or end of the day.
Ignore touts who steer you to a different boat station.
Wear sun protection, and bring water.
Avoid weekends and holidays if you can.

faq.q: How many days do you need in Ninh Binh?
faq.a: Two days lets you see the boats, the viewpoint and Hoa Lu. Many visit in a day, but it is rushed.

faq.q: Which is better, Trang An or Tam Coc?
faq.a: Trang An is more scenic, with more caves and a longer route. Tam Coc is shorter and best in rice season.

faq.q: Is Ninh Binh like Ha Long Bay?
faq.a: It has a similar limestone landscape, but on land and rivers rather than on the sea.

faq.q: What is the best time to visit?
faq.a: March to June and September to November, with golden rice in late May and June.

faq.q: How do I get there from Hanoi?
faq.a: By train or bus, about two hours.
Yes, on quiet lanes, but take care near roads.
